fiber: F_k={x in C_perp(O,r): source ray x-O lies in the closed angular cone from iota(p_k) to iota(p_(k+1))}

theorem.nonempty: every F_k contains a positive-length open source arc because det(p_k,p_(k+1))>0
theorem.connected: each F_k is one closed source arc interval
theorem.cyclic_order: F_k occur in the same cyclic order as target turns e_k
theorem.interior_disjointness: interiors of distinct F_k are disjoint
theorem.neighbor_overlap: F_(k-1) intersect F_k only at the source point on the ray through target vertex p_k; non-neighbor fibers are disjoint
theorem.fiber_boundary_count: there are exactly T_r target-vertex ray boundaries on the source circle, counted cyclically
theorem.many_to_one: for every r>=1 each target turn has an uncountable source-arc fiber while the target orbit has finitely many turns

proof_outline: AK/AL give a simple D6 cycle and a strictly angle-increasing sector path.
For each legal primitive step, the determinant with the next endpoint is strictly positive, so consecutive endpoint rays are distinct and correctly ordered.
D6 sector joins advance by exactly one sixth-turn and after six sectors return to the first ray.
Closed angular intervals between consecutive rays therefore form a cyclic interval cover of the source circle with only endpoint overlaps.
correct_comparison_unit: target elementary edge/turn; vertex fibers are tie boundaries rather than circumference units
point_fiber_warning: a vertex-only assignment would hide the continuous arc carried by each elementary target turn and is not the correct metric-descent carrier
